deckName: KS3 DT · J3 Lesson 4 · The Rescue (Teacher Deck)

slides.kicker: OUR LADY'S GRAMMAR SCHOOL · DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY
slides.heading: Lesson 4 · The Rescue
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: coming in, logging in, opening the class link. The lesson opens on the Do-Now, a short set of questions from earlier lessons that mark themselves.

SAY: "Log in, open the class link, and work through the warm-up questions on your own screen. When the screen hands you over to the story, stop and look up."

WHEN TO MOVE: when most of the room is on the story's first screen.

slides.heading: In this lesson you will…
bullets: Say why a function is better than typing the same lines again.
Write a function with a gap (a parameter) and call it with different names.
Write your own function and call it from a loop.
slides.notes: SAY these as they are written. Each one is something every pupil will have done by the end of the story.

slides.heading: Today is one story
bullets: A storm is coming. Three small animals need to get home.
You get them home by writing Python.
When your line is right, the story moves. When it is not, the card tells you what to change.
You play it on your own screen, on your own.
slides.notes:
SAY: "Today is one story, and you play it on your own. A storm is coming, and three small animals need to get home. Every part of the story moves when you type the right line. If a line is wrong, nothing bad happens: the card tells you what to change."

Headphones help if pupils have them. The story works with the sound off.

slides.heading: Start the story
bullets: Read what Blink says before you type.
More help appears each time a line is not right. Keep trying.
Need to leave the room? Press Pause the story, bottom left.
Your place is saved at every step.
slides.notes:
SAY: "Start the story now. Read what Blink says before you type. If a line is wrong, the card says what to change, and more help appears each time. If you need to leave the room, press Pause the story at the bottom left."

THEN: circulate for the rest of the hour. The river (chapter 2) and the door (chapter 4) are where pupils most often slow down.

slides.heading: The last screens
bullets: When the story ends, Blink asks 5 questions. They are marked.
Then comes the How did it go? screen. Everybody does it.
Ten minutes left and still in the story? Press the button at the bottom: Go to the 5 questions. You can go back to the story afterwards.
slides.notes: SAY: "With about ten minutes to go, if you are still in the story, press the button at the bottom that takes you to Blink's 5 questions. After them you can go back to the story. Everybody finishes the How did it go? screen."

slides.heading: Before you leave
bullets: Finish the How did it go? screen. Nobody leaves until it is done.
Sign out every time. If you do not, the next person at this computer is still signed in as you.
Your place in the story is saved.
slides.notes: SAY the sign-out line every lesson without exception. On shared C2k machines it is the single habit that matters most.
